title: The conspicuously large bracts influence reproductive success in Thunia alba (Orchidaceae)
orientation_basis: intact spur-enclosing bract constrains bypass/robbery access and shifts the same Bombus toward legitimate pollination; bract removal increases robbery
evidence_basis: Field bract-removal experiment: intact flowers received 16 normal and 3 robbery visits, versus 5 normal and 21 robbery visits after bract removal; robbed-flower fraction increased from 15.43% to 90.25%, while hourly visit frequency was unchanged.
notes: Eligibility was frozen direction-blind in Batch9. Coded as OPPOSITE/boundary relative to the focal 'legitimate-access constraint promotes bypass' prediction because this geometry primarily blocks the bypass route rather than making legitimate access harder.
